rule: Item briefs and modpools come from this mapping (zone -> skills -> tools for the job -> mods for the job), never from 'stat combo + slot'.

core.meaning: Shared mechanics near the Origin. Everyday kit any build can wear; cheapest materials (flint, bone, hide, wool, linen). Period: leans Neolithic and Chalcolithic common kit.

mid.meaning: Versatile and hybrid archetypes. The working tools of the trade (copper, early bronze, specialist organic kit). Period: Early and Middle Bronze Age.

outer.meaning: Specialised archetypes past the ring-7 class node. Full professional or high-status kit (bronze, gold, ivory, inlay); matches the class unlocks. Period: Late Bronze Age elite pieces.

confidence.A: attested: real find of this form in the period
confidence.Art: attested in period art or texts only; construction inferred
confidence.Adapt: attested elsewhere or for another use; adapted here (disclose)
confidence.Disp: object attested, but the function used here is disputed (disclose)
confidence.U: unconfirmed: do not generate without owner sign-off

globalAvoid: iron or steel look (grey sheen, fullers, crossguards); no chainmail, rivet-mail or plate armour
stitched modern soles, welts, heels, toe caps on any footwear
aprons, kilts, loincloths or hanging panels presented as body armour; belts drawn as faulds or tassets
forked or gnarled sticks as staffs or weapons; crystal-topped staffs
stone ball set in a metal cup as a 'stone mace' (real maceheads are drilled through and sit on a wooden haft)
invented-name items, lore epithets or compound coinages (owner rules 6-8)
medieval silhouettes: closed, crested, visored or nasal helmets; heater or kite shields; longswords; buckles with tongues
glass vials, potion bottles, lanterns, candles, coins, books, scrolls
glowing gems, energy veins, glow halos, floating crystals
pentagrams, rune bands, sigils, pseudo-text or pseudo-cuneiform
single boot or glove where a pair is the item; cropped cords or shafts; arrows shown in quivers (pipeline rule)

zones.role: Ritual specialist who is also healer and diviner, not a battle-mage. Evidence: shaman burials (Hilazon Tachtit c. 10,000 BC; Bad Duerrenberg c. 7000 BC; Upton Lovell G2a c. 1800 BC), Mari liver models (18th c. BC), the Ramesseum magician's box (c. 1700 BC).

No wooden frame drum survives; the clay drum stands in. Is a hide frame drum acceptable as adapted?
Hvidegaard bag contents need checking against the primary publication before a brief uses them.
Default, owner may veto (2026-11-07): period weighting by band: core leans Neolithic/Chalcolithic common kit, mid Early/Middle Bronze Age, outer Late Bronze Age elite pieces. Regions stay mixed.

zones.label: INT/DEX
zones.treeClass: ring-7 INT/DEX node: sets the INT/DEX class
zones.classUnlocks: trap and mark tools, poison vials and a supply pack
zones.wedges: poison and traps wedge (DEX toward INT/DEX): poison, wither, traps, stealth; cold and marks wedge: marks
zones.latticeRow: effect row (opened by the INT/DEX class, a wand or a knife)
zones.archetypes: blink 64/34/2, mark 53/45/2, shadow clone 49/49/2, mine 45/52/3, trap 36/61/3, poison, stealth
zones.role: Hunter-trapper and poisoner, and the night scout. Evidence: Oetzi's bast net and kit (c. 3300 BC); Egyptian clap-net fowling scenes; Border Cave and Kruger Cave poison applicators; boar's-tusk helmet of the scout. Blink, phase and shadow clone have no physical analogue; the nearest real kit is disguise (animal skins) and pigment for marks.
avoid: clay fire pots or bombs as mines (no pre-Iron-Age evidence)
open: Default, owner may veto (2026-11-07): mines are buried stake traps and laid sling shot. Clay fire pots stay out (not attested before the Iron Age). The stake bundle stays unconfirmed (not briefable) until a stake-lined pit find is cited; pit traps themselves are attested.
Default, owner may veto (2026-11-07): blink, phase and shadow clone use the disguise kit (animal skin hood, wolf skin cloak) as their visual answer.
Bronze Age arrow poison in Eurasia is not proven archaeologically; the poison container rests on southern African evidence.
Lightning spells sit here only by inference (shock support is DEX, scaling is INT). Confirm the zone before briefing their foci.

Clonbrin shield date and Sea Peoples corselet construction need primary-source checks.

Summoning: the game puts companions in the companion and Ward wedge (INT toward STR/INT), while the shared chat put summoning in pure INT. This doc follows the game.

ownerDefaults.note: Default, owner may veto (2026-11-07, via Dispatch review)
items: Horned helmet: kept only as the STR/INT outer 'Bronze horned helmet', with its cited find: the Veksø helmets, Brøns Mose, Zealand, c. 900 BC, National Museum of Denmark. STR and other zones ban fantasy (Viking-style) horned helmets.

Prefix/suffix: adopted. 2 prefixes + 2 suffixes inside the game's 4-mod limit, plus one implicit on weapon, off-hand and jewellery bases (none on body, head, hands, feet, belt). Needs a code change in Itemization.cs to take effect.
Added Fire: limited to fire-themed bases (STR/INT and the fire and ignite wedge), as mapped. This changes live drops once implemented; today the game rolls it on every weapon.
Mines: buried stake traps and laid sling shot are the period answer (Bundle of sharpened stakes, Pouch of clay sling shot). No fire pots.
Blink, phase and shadow: the disguise kit (animal skin hood, wolf skin cloak) is the visual answer.
Claws: keep the existing Bone Claws base; brief no new claw items.
Jawbone weapon: retired from new briefs (no period find). The game base and action stay as they are.
Period weighting: core leans Neolithic/Chalcolithic common kit; mid is Early/Middle Bronze Age; outer is Late Bronze Age elite pieces. Regions stay mixed.
War Horn: goes in the War Horn slot (unlocked by the STR class node), not the off hand.
Proposed mod numbers: first-pass values kept, marked provisional (status 'proposed', provisional: true).

openQuestions: No skill or item carries an attribute tag in the game code, and the owner ruled against a forced STR/DEX/INT class split (DESIGN-DIRECTION.md:432). Zone membership here is inferred from the tree's wedge themes, class nodes and the Weaving rows.
The shared chat's 303-archetype source files could not be retrieved (sandbox links). Only its published sample placements are used; the game's own skills take precedence.
Outer layer (cloak) slot exists in the game and pipeline but is not broken out per zone here; reuse the zone's body notes for mantles.
Coined pipeline names were renamed on 2026-11-07; the before and after list is owner-rules/rename-map.json.
Items marked U (unconfirmed) or with unverified precedents must not be briefed until checked; Disp items must disclose the dispute.

modpoolRules.source: Assets/ARPG/Scripts/Core/Itemization.cs:115-128 (live pool) and WizardCombat.cs (stat consumers). Live values are copied, never changed here.
modpoolRules.jobRule: A base rolls mods whose tags match the skills it serves (job, full weight), defence mods its material implies (material, full weight: metal and tusk -> Guard; hide, leather, fur, grass -> Evasion; linen, wool, felt, gold, ivory, faience -> Ward, after the PoE cloth convention), and its zone's themes (zone, 0.6 weight), plus a small shared pool (life, resistances, the zone's own attributes, and flask mods on belts; 0.5 weight). Everything else is excluded with a reason.
modpoolRules.affixCap: Default, owner may veto: 2 prefixes + 2 suffixes, inside the game's MaxModifiers 4. The game has no prefix/suffix split yet (code change needed).
modpoolRules.tiers: Tiers unlock by item level as in the game (typically ilvl 1 / 20-30 / 50-60); tier pick weights 10/5/2 (Itemization.TierWeights). A base's band sets its minimum item level: core 1, mid 15, outer 45.
modpoolRules.excluded: Each base lists the slot-eligible mods it does not roll and the tags they need; the base's skills (item.skills) carry none of those tags.
modpoolRules.weights: Mod weight = catalogue weight x role factor (job 1.0, zone 0.6, shared 0.5), so job mods dominate.
modpoolRules.implicits: Default, owner may veto: one fixed implicit per weapon, off-hand and jewellery base, taken from the base's form (spear: reach; tower shield: block and Guard). Body armour, helmets, gloves and boots carry no implicit; their base defence is the material.

status.consumer: combat already reads the stat; add the mod to the pool
status.proposed: needs a new combat consumer before it can roll; values are provisional first-pass numbers

modpoolRules.addedFire: Default, owner may veto: added-fire rolls only on fire-tagged bases (STR/INT and the fire and ignite wedge); the live game rolls it on every weapon until Itemization.cs changes.
